title: Purple Is the New Green: Is Ube the Next Matcha?
paragraphs: Bright purple drinks and desserts have been appearing in cafes and dessert spots around the world. And their color comes from an ingredient that has been part of Filipino cooking for thousands of years.
It's called ube, a type of yam with a mild sweetness and a naturally purple color. In the Philippines, it's traditionally used to make jams and desserts.
But now, ube is finding new fans far beyond its home country.

In March 2026, major coffee chains including Starbucks and Costa Coffee introduced ube drinks in several countries, including the UK and the US. And in South Korea, the coffee chain Paik's Coffee started selling ube lattes and ice cream in May.
It's not just the big chains that are joining the trend, either.
In Tokyo, independent coffee shop Studio Cafe Maru has also been selling ube cheesecakes and lattes since May. The cafe says its sales have increased by about 50% since then.
So what's behind this growing interest?
Part of the answer is social media. Ube's bright purple color makes drinks and desserts stand out in photos, helping them attract attention online.
But its taste is important too.

Speaking to FNN Prime Online, customers at Studio Cafe Maru described the ube desserts as sweet and smooth, with a mild flavor. One customer said they had expected a strong yam flavor, but were surprised by how mild it tasted.
Food journalist Mayumi Satoi told FNN Prime Online that ube's mild sweetness works well with other ingredients, making it easy for chefs to use in different drinks and desserts.
Ube also contains dietary fiber, giving it a reputation as a healthy ingredient.
Food experts are comparing ube's growing international appeal with that of matcha, Japan's famous green tea powder.
Of course, it's too early to say whether ube's popularity will be as long-lasting as matcha's. But with more cafes adding it to their menus, the purple yam is certainly getting noticed!
